turns.content: A very large gene contains many exons encoding repeated rod-like domains that connect the cytoskeleton to the sarcolemma; frame-shifting exon deletions cause progressive muscle degeneration. Identify the gene and disease.
A Morpholino binds the 5' end of an out-of-frame exon in the pre-mRNA and blocks spliceosome access. Explain the therapeutic strategy and its immediate RNA-level effect.
Why can skipping one additional exon restore the reading frame and produce a shorter but partly functional dystrophin rather than simply worsening the deletion?

During transcription, nascent RNA can hybridize to template DNA while displacing the non-template strand. Describe this three-stranded structure and distinguish it from a spliceosomal lariat and Morpholino-pre-mRNA binding.
Name that transcription-associated structure and explain why it is not required for Morpholino exon-skipping therapy.
